widgets_values_named.h3_preview:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Stylized 3D CG comedic animation, a medium shot opens on the man exactly as shown in <Picture 1> — neon green buzzcut, mirrored wraparound visor sunglasses worn even at this sleepy hour, a single pearl drop earring on his right ear only with the left ear bare, and the same eye shape and head structure — sitting slumped on the edge of a messy bed in rumpled pajamas inside a 90s metalhead bedroom cluttered with band posters. He yawns and rubs his face, looking extremely sleepy, then the drowsy, low-pitched young man (S1) mutters: <d>[English] Five more minutes... no, wait, I'm already up.</d> He stretches both arms overhead, pushes himself upright, and shuffles right toward the bathroom door as the camera tracks right with small amplitude at a steady pace, following him past the doorway into the bathroom. He steps up to the mirror and looks straight into the camera as if meeting his own reflection, lifts the hem of his pajama top with one hand, and sprays deodorant under the raised arm with the other, wincing slightly at the cold mist. He sets the deodorant on the sink edge, reaches to the opposite side for a bottle of mouthwash, takes a sip, gargles loudly with puffed cheeks, and spits it into the sink, shaking his head once as (S1) grumbles: <d>[English] Ugh, that's freezing.</d> Wiping his mouth with the back of his hand, he turns and walks right again toward the kitchen while the camera continues its rightward tracking motion, arriving at a kitchen counter that fills the foreground as he pulls out a stool and sits, reaching for a box of cereal beside a chipped mug. [Shot 2] At 00:13.500, the shot cuts to a tight close-up on his visor sunglasses as a cereal flake bounces off the lens, and (S1) deadpans: <d>[English] Really, again?</d>

overall_soundscape: Bedsprings creak and fabric rustles as he stretches, followed by soft footsteps padding across a hallway floor. The deodorant can hisses briefly, liquid sloshes and gargles in the bathroom, then splashes into the sink basin. In the kitchen, a stool scrapes the floor, a cereal box crinkles, and a single flake clinks lightly off glass.

non_diegetic_music: A playful, palm-muted electric guitar riff at a moderate tempo drives the sequence, underscored by a tight, syncopated drum groove. A single staccato guitar chord and a snare hit accent the cut to the close-up at the end.

nodes.title: H3 Characters — custom performer + wardrobe

widgets_values:
# H3 Music Video

1. **Load the song** → `audio` of the **H3 Music Video Writer** (and `replace_audio` of H3 Scenes Join, so the finished video carries the original track).
2. The writer cuts the song into 5–15 s pieces on the music (timed lyrics make cuts land before lines), writes one scene per piece with `<Audio 1>` = that piece, and emits matching lists: `scenes` → prompt, `lengths` → length (frame counts on H3's grid), `audio_segments` → `ref_audio_1`.
3. The H3 video node runs once per piece and each clip is DECODED AND SAVED as its own video file (VAE Decode → Create Video → Save Video). Stitch externally, or re-add **H3 Scenes Join** before Create Video for one file with the original song.

Put lyrics with timestamps (`[0:12] line`) for exact lip-sync; a custom performer + wardrobe comes from the H3 Characters node (✏️ custom). Connect reference images (the performer's face) to the writer's `image_1..` and they reach the video node and the preview thumbnails.

**Seed:** the writer's seed is **-1 (randomize)** - every queue writes a brand-new video; nothing is reused from earlier runs. To use the Review node's stop-edit-**Continue** flow, first set the writer's seed to a FIXED number: Continue relies on ComfyUI reusing the cached scenes, and with -1 each queue writes fresh scenes and re-reviews instead.

**Original sound:** every saved clip carries its ORIGINAL slice of the song (the writer's `audio_segments`, cut on the same frame grid) - not the model-generated audio, and in the masked workflow not the vocals-only stem. Wire Create Video's `audio` back to VAE Decode Audio if you want to hear what the model generated.

**Turbo variant:** the render chain carries the speed setup from the reference graph - `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema.safetensors` LoRA, chunked feed-forward, Sage + LowVRAM + SoL attention, EasyCache and Spectrum, sampled with euler at 4 steps. Needs the packs providing those nodes (Spectrum-MiniMax-H3, the SoL/turbo patch packs) and the turbo LoRA in models/loras.

**What H3 listens to - Voice Over Music.** The audio in H3's latent is not the song itself but a mix made for the model: AudioSeparation's **Vocals** on top at full level, **Drums + Bass + Other** summed **-9 dB** under them and ducked a further **-6 dB** only while the voice sounds. The mouth follows the voice, the picture moves on the real beat, and no word gets buried (the plain song buried consonants; the bare vocal stem had no beat to cut on). `music_db` is the dial: -3 is nearly the full song, -18 a whisper of beat. The original song still goes to the output.

**Beats.** Sound Events (hits, drops, stops) → **Beat Grid** (the tempo and every beat, phase-fitted to the hits) → **Cut Plan** (the scenes, cut on the music) → the writer's `cut_plan` and `sound_events`. Every piece's brief then lists its `[beat]` offsets and its `[+start ->+land ->+settle s]` moments, and the scene is staged on them - the hit sentences are written ON TOP of the piece's picture budget, never instead of it.

**Clips land one by one.** The sampler and Save Clip are one node here - **Sampler + Save Clip** - so every scene is sampled, decoded, muxed with its slice of the song and written to `output/` BEFORE the next scene starts sampling. Watch the folder fill up during the run; a crash late in the run keeps everything already saved. (Two separate nodes would sample every scene first and only then start saving.)

nodes.title: H3 Music Video Writer
Masked-audio lip-sync
widgets_values:
**Masked-audio music video** - the strongest lip-sync H3 can do.

Each clip's exact slice of the song is encoded with the audio VAE and written straight into the H3 audio latent, protected from denoising (mask 0). The video is generated against the real, frozen vocal - lip-sync is enforced by the model, not requested by the prompt.

- The song is **not** connected to `ref_audio` (that is on purpose).
- The **vocal stem** (AudioSeparation) is injected so instruments don't mask the voice; the final soundtrack is still the full mix via Scenes Join `replace_audio`.
- The writer's `audio_mode` is set to *Masked latent*, so the prompts reference the protected master-song audio instead of `<Audio 1>`.
- `clip_starts` from the writer gives every clip its exact offset in the master song.

Needs audio-separation-nodes-comfyui (the masked-audio node is this pack's own H3 Masked Song Latent).
